title.en: Language work for the poem on the magic brush: draw, interjections, falling tone and imaginative essay

text.en: A poem about a magic brush brings us to a word with many meanings, short words of feeling, the tone of a command and a creative essay.

keepEnglishTerms: Phew, Eek, Ouch, Yippee, Whoa, Oops, Hey
draw: get a reaction, attract, absorb

text.en:
The verb draw has different meanings in different contexts. A speech can draw loud applause (get a reaction), an event can draw huge crowds (attract), and plants draw water (absorb) from the soil.
A train draws into the station (moving), she drew the curtains (opened them), and he drew a paper from the folder (pulled it out). Always decide the meaning from the sentence.
Interjections show sudden feelings. Phew! shows relief, Eek! alarm, Ouch! pain, Yippee! delight, Whoa! surprise, Oops! a mistake and Hey! attracts attention.
In a sentence, the interjection is followed by an exclamation mark: 'Ouch! I hurt my finger' and 'Yippee! We won the match'.
Intonation is the rise and fall of the pitch of your voice. The falling tone drops from a high level to a low level and is generally used in imperative sentences, such as commands, instructions, requests for a favour or warnings.
Read these with a falling tone: 'Come here!', 'Seize this magic brush', 'Paint my fortress tall!' and 'Go and fetch some rice'. Take turns making formal and informal requests in pairs.
An imaginative essay is a creative piece that uses imagination. It can be based on real-life events, observation or experience, and is usually a descriptive piece or a personal reflection. A good one starts with a hook, like 'Imagine an ordinary 13-year-old who is also a secret superhero'.
To plan your essay: pick a character or idea, describe the powers or setting, show a problem and how it is solved, and end with what you learnt or feel.

problem.en: Match the meaning of 'draw' in: (a) 'Plants draw water from the soil.' (b) 'She drew the curtains.' Then pick an interjection for dropping a glass.

prompt.en: Explain the falling tone and when it is used, and give two interjections with their emotions.

requiredIdeas.en: The pitch falls from high to low
It is used for commands, instructions, requests and warnings
Phew! shows relief and Ouch! shows pain

commonMisconceptions.en: Using a rising tone for commands
Forgetting the exclamation mark after an interjection
